title: Chapter 136 — Online Reviews & Reputation
intro: One bad Google review can cost you more than a hundred good sales days.

sections.title: Responding to Negative Reviews
sections.content:
Never get defensive. Never argue. Never blame the customer. The potential customers reading your response are not judging whether you were right — they are evaluating how you handle problems.

Template: 'Thank you for sharing your experience, [name]. I am sorry we did not meet your expectations. I would like to make this right — please call me directly at [number] so I can help.' Three elements: acknowledge, apologize, offer resolution. Take it offline. Resolve it privately. Then the customer often updates or removes the review.

Never respond when you are angry. Write the draft. Wait an hour. Read it as if you are a potential customer seeing it for the first time. Then edit. The response you write at 8 AM when you are calm is always better than the one you write at 9 PM when you are frustrated.

sections.title: Building a Review Culture
sections.content:
Do not wait for reviews to happen organically — they skew negative because unhappy customers are 3-5 times more likely to leave a review than happy ones. Build a system that captures the happy customers.

Ask every satisfied customer at the right moment — 48 hours to one week after delivery. Send the direct link. Make it one click. 'Would you mind leaving a quick review? It helps our store and it helps me personally.'

The math of reviews: a store with 50 five-star reviews and one 1-star review has a 4.9 rating. A store with 5 five-star reviews and one 1-star review has a 4.2 rating. Volume protects you from the occasional inevitable complaint. Build the volume proactively instead of waiting for the bad ones to define you.

sections.title: What Never to Say Publicly
sections.content:
Never disclose customer details in a public response. Never admit specific liability or fault in writing — 'we caused the damage' is a legal statement. Never promise specific compensation publicly — 'I will give you a full refund' sets expectations for every future reviewer. Never argue with the reviewer, even when they are factually wrong.

Keep public responses short, empathetic, and focused on moving the conversation offline. Everything you write is permanent and visible to every future customer who Googles your store. Write accordingly.
